The table of contents places Chapter 7 'The Hook Formula' at printed p. 27 and Chapter 8 'The RSK Correspondence' at printed p. 29. Read both chapters in full: the recursion f^lambda = sum_i f^{lambda minus i}; Remark 7.1 (Vandermonde Delta_k and the Young-Frobenius expression f-tilde); Lemma 7.2 and Theorem 7.3(a)(b); the hook formula; the insertion map ins and Lemma 8.1, Theorem 8.2; Remark 8.3 (ins(sigma^{-1})=(Q,P), the P=Q characterization of involutions, and the bound sum_lambda f^lambda, citing Sagan Theorem 3.6.6); Algorithm 8.4 with Example 8.5; Theorems 8.6, 8.7 (inverse algorithms); Algorithm 8.8, Theorem 8.9 (bijection), Corollary 8.10, Example 8.11. sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete article PDF (1,984,341 bytes, 23 pages including the journal cover and back matter) and extracted its full text with mutool. Read §§2-4, printed pp. 711-720, in full: the bordered-array convention and the INSERT (x) and DELETE (s,t) algorithms with their parenthesized invariants; the proof that INSERT and DELETE are inverse; Theorem 1 (x<x' iff s>s' iff t>t') with its two induction parts; the matrix/two-line-array dictionary and the lexicographic ordering convention; construction A (insert v_k, write u_k at the new box (s_k,t_k)) and construction B (delete the rightmost largest entry of Q, DELETE the corresponding box of P); Theorem 2; the inversion digraph D_1 with the arc condition u<=u' and v<=v'; the source-stripping classes and Lemma 1 (by induction on N) describing the first rows of P and Q; the second-order digraph D_{i+1} construction and its use for the remaining rows; the Corollary on longest nondecreasing subsequences; Theorem 3, that A^T corresponds to (Q,P), with its proof from the line-swap isomorphism of the digraphs; and Theorem 4. Skimmed §§5-7, printed pp. 720-727, for the dual correspondence, the plactic Theorems 5-6 and the Littlewood identity, and recorded dispositions for them. Repair reviewer independently re-fetched the complete23-page PDF (1984341bytes, SHA25624110cfb5d82f47915b75583a696f01678fb83e05676c415c69c8e0151203cbc), extracted every page, and read §§2–4, pp711–719: INSERT/DELETE assertions, weak ordered-input comparison, first-row source-layer lemma and shifted-pair recursion. Repaired RSK item explicitly reverses within-layer order after coordinate swapping and proves the bump-array comparison rather than asserting it.

contents.name: Theorem 3: A^T corresponds to (Q,P)

contents.reason: The symmetric-matrix specialization and its odd-column trace statistic are not among the pair's commissioned claims; the P=Q principle used for involutions is taken from the permutation specialization instead.

contents.reason: Dual (column-insertion) RSK for zero-one matrices is not used by the permutation or two-line-array statements of this pair; only the commutation Lemma 6 of Schensted quotes the dual algorithm.

contents.name: §6 Theorems 5-6 (plactic equivalence and the invariance of the P-tableau)
contents.reason: The plactic monoid and the elementary-transformation characterization are not needed for the hook formula, the RSK bijection or the subsequence theorem; the pair records them here as declined source content.
